chunks: And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

During the time of ‘Alī عليه السلام, a man had two female slaves, and both gave birth on the same night, one of them to a son and the other to a daughter. Then the mother of the daughter deliberately placed her daughter in the cradle in which the son had been, and took the son; so the mother of the daughter said, “The son is my son,” and the mother of the son said, “The son is my son.” So they sought judgment from Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام, and he ordered that their milk be weighed, and he said, “Whichever of the two has the heavier milk, then the son belongs to her.”

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ‘Alī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الِابْنُ: the son whose maternity was disputed
key_terms.الْمَهْدِ: the cradle in which the infant was placed
key_terms.جَارِيَتَانِ: two female slaves owned by the same man
key_terms.فَتَحَاكَمَا: they brought their dispute for legal judgment
key_terms.لَبَنُهُمَا: the milk of the two women
key_terms.يُوزَنَ: to be weighed as a means of determining the case

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ‘Alī عليه السلام judge a case when two women both claimed the same infant boy?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling by Amīr al-Mu’minīn ‘Alī عليه السلام in a maternity dispute between two slave women who had given birth on the same night. He resolved the case by ordering their milk to be weighed and assigning the boy to the woman whose milk was heavier, illustrating practical adjudication in a disputed matter of lineage and motherhood.
